status: completed local diagnostic; no shipping configuration changed
lock_initialization: Copied the shipping Cargo.lock into the local package, then one local unlocked hardware-feature build added sha2-asm 0.6.4. Final software and hardware binaries were built --locked against the same local lock. Shipping Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock were unchanged.

features.hardware: same plus asm -> sha2-asm 0.6.4; aarch64 backend detects sha2 at runtime; detected true

identity_validation.hash_order: BTreeMap node order; SHA256 concatenation of u32LE encoded length and Node::encode() for every node, plus separate SHA256 of Manifest::encode()
identity_validation.byte_reconstruction: Every graph was strictly rebuilt and compared byte-for-byte to its input before timing in both executable runs

measurements: One warmup, seven sequential samples per operation; 100 operations per sample only for object hash and copy; allocation/drop included; identical source and fixtures.
interpretation: Whole-object SHA and all-node-ID hashing improved in this run, but full random Graph::fold became slower. No end-to-end DAG improvement is established.

Several non-hash controls also slowed in the hardware run. Sequential software-then-hardware order on an unisolated host cannot distinguish host scheduling/frequency/memory effects from feature/codegen effects.
The original packet is preserved unchanged; its checksums all verified before this experiment.
This is not a WAN rerun, full shipping test qualification, energy measurement, or FIPS validation.
